surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Capitals beat the Rangers
paras: Alexis Lafrenière opened the scoring for the Rangers on the power play midway through the first, and that was all they would get. Timothy Liljegren tied it up for Washington early in the second. Igor Shesterkin left the game in the second, and Dylan Garand finished it in net for the Rangers. Boone Jenner scored his first goal for Washington late in the second to put the Capitals ahead for good. Tom Wilson added the empty-netter with just one second left to make it 3-1.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. Logan Thompson made 21 saves for the Capitals. The Caps improved to 3-1-0, third in the Metropolitan, while the Rangers dropped to 4-2-0, tied for first in the NHL in points.

items.text: The Rangers’ four-game winning streak is over.
With Matt Roy out, Liljegren took his spot and scored.
Adam Fox and Gabe Perreault saw their point streaks end.
Both of the preview’s calls held.
